parameters.content:
## Data centre moratorium tracker (Gemini) — setup

1. **Config** node: replace `CHANGE-ME@example.com` with the address that should get the digest. `model` is the Gemini model; if the test run says the model isn't found, copy a current model name from Google AI Studio.
2. **Classify with Gemini**: create a *Header Auth* credential. Name: `x-goog-api-key`, Value: your Gemini API key (aistudio.google.com → Get API key).
3. **Read existing rows** and **Log to Google Sheet**: connect your Google account (same credential for both). The sheet is already set.
4. **Email digest**: connect Gmail.
5. Click **Execute workflow** once to test, then toggle the workflow **Active**.

Runs every 2 days at 07:00 Madrid time and searches the last 72 hours (stories already in the sheet are skipped). Headlines go to Gemini one at a time (about 10 a minute) to stay inside the free tier's rate limit, so a full run takes up to ~7 minutes.
Rows already in the sheet are never added again, even after moving to a new n8n account.

An email is sent after every run with a run report (headlines found, sent to Gemini, Gemini errors). To catch up after a gap, set `lookbackHours` in Config to e.g. 504 (21 days) and raise `maxItemsPerRun`, run once, then set them back.

parameters.jsCode:
return [{ json: {
  // ---- EDIT THESE ----
  notifyEmail: 'CHANGE-ME@example.com', // replace with the address that should get the digest
  lookbackHours: 72,          // how far back to search (runs are 48h apart; the overlap catches late-listed stories). For a one-off catch-up run set e.g. 504 (21 days), then set back to 72
  maxItemsPerRun: 60,         // cap on items sent to Gemini per run (stays well inside free-tier daily limits)
  confidenceThreshold: 0.6,   // minimum classifier confidence to log an action
  model: 'gemini-flash-latest', // any Gemini model name from Google AI Studio
  // --------------------
  systemPrompt: "You classify news items for a tracker of government actions that restrict new data centre construction anywhere in the world.

Return ONLY a JSON object, with no prose and no code fences.

COUNT as a moratorium action: a government body, regulator, planning authority or grid operator adopting, proposing, extending, lifting or rejecting a moratorium, ban, pause, freeze, or blanket refusal of new data centre permits or grid connections. Votes by residents on a ban also count.

DO NOT count: opinion pieces or analysis with no specific new action; the rejection of a single project; bans that only cover crypto mining; general energy or efficiency rules that do not pause development; articles that only recap older actions with no new development.

Schema:
{
  "is_moratorium_action": boolean,
  "action_type": "adopted" | "proposed" | "extended" | "lifted" | "rejected" | "ban" | "other",
  "jurisdiction": string (US places as 'City, ST' or 'County Name, ST' with the two-letter state code, e.g. 'Manatee County, FL'; US states by full name; elsewhere the official name of the place or body),
  "level": "city" | "county" | "region" | "state" | "national" | "grid_operator",
  "country": string (English name),
  "scope": string (what is paused, e.g. 'new data centres over 50 MW', or '' if unknown),
  "effective_date": string or null (YYYY-MM-DD),
  "expiry": string or null,
  "summary": string (start with 'Status: active.', 'Status: proposed.', 'Status: rejected.', 'Status: lifted.' or 'Status: expired.', then one sentence in English),
  "confidence": number between 0 and 1
}

If the item is not in English, write every field in English. If is_moratorium_action is false, the other fields can be empty strings or null."
} }];

parameters.name: query
parameters.value: ("data center" OR "data centre" OR datacenter) (moratorium OR ban OR freeze)

Snippet: ' + ($json.snippet || '') + '
Published: ' + ($json.published || 'unknown') + '
URL: ' + $json.link }] }], generationConfig: { responseMimeType: 'application/json', temperature: 0, maxOutputTokens: 4096 } }) }}
